examples.en: I was constantly touching my phone without realizing it.

examples.ko: 무의식중에 아버지와 똑같은 말을 해 버렸어요.
examples.en: Without thinking, I said exactly the same thing my father says.

examples.ko: 시험 볼 때 무의식중에 손톱을 물어뜯어요.
examples.en: When I take tests, I bite my nails without meaning to.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 무의식중에 속마음을 말해 버렸어요.
examples.en: That friend let slip what was on their mind without thinking.

examples.ko: 무의식중에 한 행동이라서 잘 기억이 안 나요.
examples.en: It was something I did unconsciously, so I don't remember it well.

examples.ko: 저는 무의식중에 노래를 따라 부르고 있었어요.
examples.en: I was singing along without even noticing.

explain: 거의 항상 '무의식중에'처럼 '에'를 붙여 부사처럼 써요. '나도 모르게', '저도 모르게'와 뜻이 비슷한데, 일상 대화에서는 그 말을 더 자주 하고 '무의식중에'는 조금 더 글 같은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with '에' as '무의식중에', working like an adverb. It is close to '나도 모르게' (without realizing), but people say that more in daily talk, while '무의식중에' sounds a bit more written.

examples.ko: 처음에 실패해도 그 경험이 무익하지는 않을 거예요.
examples.en: Even if you fail at first, that experience won't be useless.
That kind of fight does no good for either side.
I want to stop this pointless argument now.

examples.ko: 준비 없이 하는 노력은 무익할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Effort without preparation can be futile.
That meeting only took up time and was of no use.

examples.ko: 지금 걱정만 하는 건 무익하다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think just worrying right now is of no use.

explain: 반대말은 '유익하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '소용없다', '쓸모없다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '무익하다'는 글이나 격식 있는 말에서 자주 나와요. '무익하지 않다'처럼 부정하면 '꽤 도움이 된다'는 조심스러운 칭찬이 돼요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '유익하다' (beneficial). In daily talk people more often say '소용없다' or '쓸모없다', while '무익하다' shows up in writing and formal speech. Negating it, as in '무익하지 않다', becomes a careful way of saying something is quite useful.

examples.en: I lost my wallet and ended up without a penny.
He came up to Seoul without a penny to his name.
It's before payday, so I'm almost broke right now.
Starting from nothing, I opened a small shop.

examples.ko: 친구가 무일푼인 저에게 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: A friend bought me a meal since I was penniless.
Even without a penny, my mind is at ease.

explain: 돈이 한 푼도 없는 상태를 말하고, '무일푼이 되다', '무일푼으로 시작하다'처럼 자주 써요. 사람을 가리켜 말할 때는 '빈털터리'라는 말도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes having no money at all and is common in patterns like '무일푼이 되다' (end up penniless) and '무일푼으로 시작하다' (start from nothing). When talking about a person, Koreans also often say '빈털터리' (a broke person).

examples.ko: 무자격자는 이 일을 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Unqualified people can't do this job.
You must not leave surgery to someone who isn't qualified.
I heard that academy had an instructor without credentials.

examples.ko: 무자격자가 운전을 하면 큰 사고가 나요.
examples.en: If an unlicensed person drives, a serious accident can happen.
A company that hired unqualified people was on the news.
I asked whether people without qualifications can apply too.

explain: 반대말은 '유자격자'예요. 자격증이나 필요한 자격 없이 일하는 사람을 가리킬 때 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '자격이 없는 사람'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요. 뉴스나 안내문에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '유자격자' (a qualified person). It points to someone working without the required license or qualification, and in daily talk people may spell it out as '자격이 없는 사람'. You see it often in news and notices.

examples.en: My grandmother lived alone all her life with no children.
My friend has no children, so she adores her nephew.
That couple has no children but lives happily.
They say that in the old days, families without children worried a lot.
I went to a group that helps elderly people with no children.

examples.ko: 무자식이 되고 싶어서 된 건 아니에요.
examples.en: It's not that I wanted to have no children.

explain: 자식이 없다는 사실을 조금 딱딱하게 말하는 단어예요. 사람 앞에서 말할 때는 '자녀가 없다'가 더 부드럽게 들려요. '무자식 상팔자'라는 속담으로 가장 많이 만나요.

phrases.example: 아이 키우느라 힘들 때마다 부모님은 무자식 상팔자라고 말씀하세요.
phrases.en: No children is the best fortune.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자식 걱정이 끊이지 않으니 차라리 자식이 없는 게 편하다는 속담이에요. 진심이라기보다 힘들 때 푸념하듯 말하는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that children bring endless worry, so having none is easier. It is usually a half-joking complaint rather than a sincere belief.

explain_en: It states the fact of having no children in a rather blunt way. When speaking about a person, '자녀가 없다' sounds softer. You most often meet it in the proverb '무자식 상팔자'.

examples.en: In college, I set off on a no-money trip with a friend.

examples.ko: 요즘은 무전여행을 하는 사람이 많지 않아요.
examples.en: These days not many people travel without money.

examples.ko: 무전여행 중에 낯선 아주머니가 밥을 주셨어요.
examples.en: During the trip, a stranger woman gave me a meal.
I heard my father even went on no-money trips when he was young.

examples.ko: 돈 없이 가는 무전여행은 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A trip with no money can be dangerous.
A trip with no money? That's really brave of you.

explain: 돈을 거의 안 가지고 다른 사람의 도움으로 먹고 자며 다니는 여행이에요. 돈을 쓰되 싸게 다니는 '배낭여행'과는 달라요. 요즘은 위험해서 드물고, 옛날이야기나 추억담에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means travelling with almost no money, relying on others' help for food and a place to sleep. It differs from '배낭여행' (backpacking), where you still spend money but cheaply. It is rare today because of the risks and mostly comes up in old stories and memories.

examples.en: If you live without restraint, your health gets worse.

examples.ko: 그는 월급을 무절제하게 써서 늘 돈이 없어요.
examples.en: He spends his pay recklessly, so he's always out of money.

examples.ko: 밤마다 무절제하게 먹다가 살이 많이 쪘어요.
examples.en: I ate with no self-control every night and gained a lot of weight.
My lifestyle has been way too undisciplined lately.

examples.ko: 무절제한 인터넷 사용이 문제가 되고 있어요.
examples.en: Unrestrained internet use is becoming a problem.
My life is so undisciplined that I'm tired every morning.

explain: 반대말은 '절제하다'예요. 먹기, 돈 쓰기, 인터넷 사용처럼 정도를 지키지 못하는 일에 '무절제하게 + 동사'로 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '마구', '함부로', '제멋대로'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '절제하다' (to restrain oneself). It is often used as '무절제하게 + verb' for things where someone fails to keep limits, like eating, spending or internet use. In daily talk people also say '마구', '함부로' or '제멋대로'.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 무주택이라서 청약을 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I don't own a home yet, so I'm looking into the housing subscription.
They say households without a home get the chance first.
The longer you've gone without owning a home, the higher your score.
Many newlyweds don't own a home.

examples.ko: 무주택자를 위한 대출 상품이 새로 나왔어요.
examples.en: A new loan product for people without a home has come out.
Many people have gone a long time without owning a home.

explain: 자기 집이 없다는 뜻이라서 '무주택자', '무주택 가구'로 뉴스나 청약 안내에서 많이 나와요. 길에서 사는 '노숙'과는 달라서, 월세나 전세로 살아도 무주택이에요. 반대말은 '유주택'이에요.
explain_en: It means not owning a home, and appears in news and housing-subscription notices as '무주택자' or '무주택 가구'. It is different from sleeping on the street: someone renting on 월세 or 전세 is still 무주택. The opposite is '유주택'.

examples.en: The inside of a space station is in a weightless state.
In zero gravity, water floats around in round blobs.

examples.ko: 무중력 체험 영상을 봤는데 정말 신기했어요.
examples.en: I watched a zero-gravity experience video and it was really amazing.
Astronauts train in weightless conditions.
When there's no gravity, your body floats up.
Lying on the bed, my body feels light as if in zero gravity.

explain: '무중력 상태'로 가장 자주 쓰고, 과학 기사나 우주 영상에서 많이 나와요. 우주선 안에서는 중력이 완전히 없다기보다 몸이 떠다녀서 무게를 못 느끼는 것이라 '무중량'이라고도 해요. 몸이 붕 뜬 것처럼 가볍고 편한 기분은 '무중력 같다'고 비유해요.
explain_en: It is most often used as '무중력 상태' and appears in science news and space videos. In a spacecraft gravity does not fully vanish; you simply float and feel no weight, which is why '무중량' (weightlessness) is also used. A light, floating, comfortable feeling is described figuratively as '무중력 같다'.

examples.en: That person is incredibly, brutishly strong.
A tremendous downpour came and the roads were blocked.
I was shocked to see my friend eat so ferociously.

examples.ko: 선생님이 숙제를 무지막지하게 많이 내 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher gave us an insanely large amount of homework.
The price was outrageous, so I just left.
I carried a ridiculously heavy load by myself.

explain: 원래는 거칠고 무례하다는 뜻인데, 요즘은 양이나 힘, 가격이 어이없을 만큼 대단할 때도 많이 써요. 보통 좋은 느낌은 아니고 '너무하다'는 마음이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: Originally it describes someone rough and rude, but today it is also often used when amount, strength or price is shockingly extreme. It usually carries a negative 'that's too much' feeling rather than praise.

examples.en: It's insanely hot today.
This tteokbokki is super spicy.
Yesterday's test was really, really hard.
I've missed you so much all this time.
I like that singer a whole lot.
The baby grows up incredibly fast.

explain: '아주', '정말'을 강하게 말하는 구어체 부사예요. 친구끼리나 편한 자리에서 쓰고, 글이나 발표에서는 '매우'가 더 어울려요. 더 짧게 '무지'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a spoken adverb that intensifies '아주' or '정말'. Use it with friends or in casual settings; in writing or presentations '매우' fits better. It can also be shortened to '무지'.

examples.ko: 이 약은 무지무지하게 써서 먹기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This medicine is so incredibly bitter that it's hard to take.

examples.ko: 무지무지한 눈이 쏟아져서 차가 못 다녀요.
examples.en: Enormous amounts of snow are falling, so cars can't get through.

examples.ko: 그 가게 앞에 무지무지하게 긴 줄이 있어요.
examples.en: There's an incredibly long line in front of that shop.

examples.ko: 이번 달 일이 무지무지해서 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: This month's workload is enormous, so I'm overwhelmed.
A huge crowd gathered at the amusement park.
Everyone is worn out from the tremendous heat.

explain: 양이나 정도가 어마어마할 때 쓰는 구어체 말이에요. '무지무지한 + 명사', '무지무지하게 + 서술어'로 쓰고, '엄청나다'와 비슷하지만 말하듯 가벼운 느낌이에요. 부사 '무지무지'는 따로 있어서 '무지무지 덥다'처럼 바로 붙여요.
explain_en: It is a spoken word for when an amount or degree is enormous. It is used as '무지무지한 + noun' or '무지무지하게 + predicate', and is similar to '엄청나다' but with a lighter, chatty feel. The adverb '무지무지' is a separate word, used directly as in '무지무지 덥다'.

examples.ko: 결과가 너무 무참해서 말이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The result is so crushing that I'm speechless.
The players hung their heads after the crushing defeat.
The accident scene was almost too grim to look at.
The merciless criticism hurt me a lot.
The sight was so wretched that I looked away.

examples.ko: 무참하게 무너진 집을 보니 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: It breaks my heart to see the house so utterly ruined.

explain: '참혹하다'와 비슷하게 보기 끔찍하고 안타까운 상황에 쓰는 말이에요. 형용사로 쓰기보다 '무참히', '무참하게'처럼 부사로 말할 때가 더 많아요. 일상 대화보다는 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Like '참혹하다', it describes terrible, pitiful situations. It is more often used adverbially, as '무참히' or '무참하게', than as a plain adjective. You see it more in news and writing than in everyday talk.

examples.en: That promise was brutally broken.
My hopes were utterly crushed, and I'm upset.
Our team lost by a crushing margin.
The beautiful forest was mercilessly cut down.
I was ruthlessly betrayed by someone I trusted.
His dream was cruelly trampled.

explain: 깨지다, 무너지다, 짓밟히다, 지다처럼 나쁜 일을 당하는 말과 잘 어울려요. 좋은 일에는 쓰지 않고, 안타깝고 끔찍하다는 느낌이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It pairs well with words about bad things happening, like 깨지다, 무너지다, 짓밟히다 and 지다. It is never used for good things and carries a feeling of pity and horror.

examples.ko: 그는 검은색이나 회색 같은 무채색을 좋아해요.
examples.en: He likes achromatic colors like black and gray.
Neutral-colored clothes go well with anything.

examples.ko: 제 방은 흰색과 회색 같은 무채색이에요.
examples.en: My room is in neutral colors like white and gray.

examples.ko: 미술 시간에 무채색과 유채색의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In art class, we learned the difference between achromatic and chromatic colors.

examples.ko: 무채색 가구에 노란 쿠션으로 포인트를 줬어요.
examples.en: I added an accent with a yellow cushion on the neutral-colored furniture.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 무채색 코트를 입는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: In winter, many people wear neutral-colored coats.

explain: 흰색, 회색, 검은색처럼 색깔이 없는 색이고, 반대말은 '유채색'이에요. 패션이나 인테리어에서는 '무채색 계열'이라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It covers colors without hue, like white, gray and black; the opposite is '유채색' (chromatic color). In fashion and interior design, people often say '무채색 계열' (neutral-tone range).

examples.en: A jellyfish is an invertebrate.
Insects and shellfish are among the invertebrates.
In science class, we tried classifying invertebrates.
Octopuses are invertebrates too.
I watched a video observing invertebrates under the sea.

examples.ko: 무척추동물은 척추 대신 껍데기가 있는 경우도 있어요.
examples.en: Some invertebrates have a shell instead of a backbone.

explain: 반대말은 '척추동물'이에요. 곤충, 조개, 오징어, 해파리처럼 등뼈가 없는 동물을 묶어 부르는 과학 용어라서 수업이나 책에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '척추동물' (vertebrate). It is a science term grouping animals without a backbone, like insects, clams, squid and jellyfish, so it comes up often in class and books.

examples.en: We don't have unlimited time.

examples.ko: 이 일을 무한정 기다릴 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I can't wait for this forever.

examples.ko: 이 서비스는 무한정 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this service without limit.

examples.ko: 돈이 무한정 나오는 기계가 있으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish there were a machine that gave out endless money.
I'm exhausted by the endlessly growing workload.

examples.ko: 음식을 무한정 시켜 먹을 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't order food endlessly.

explain: '무한정 기다리다', '무한정 쓰다'처럼 부사처럼 동사 앞에 붙여 쓸 때가 가장 많아요. '끝없이', '한없이'와 비슷하지만 '횟수나 양에 제한이 없다'는 느낌이 강하고, '~ㄹ 수는 없다' 같은 부정 표현과 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is mostly used like an adverb before a verb, as in '무한정 기다리다' or '무한정 쓰다'. It is similar to '끝없이' and '한없이', but stresses that there is no limit on amount or number, and it often appears with negatives like '~ㄹ 수는 없다'.

examples.en: Unauthorized buildings can be torn down.
It was an unlicensed shop, so it got caught in a crackdown.
If you do business without a license, you have to pay a fine.

examples.ko: 무허가 약을 사지 말라고 뉴스에서 말했어요.
examples.en: The news said not to buy unapproved medicine.
I heard this neighborhood used to have many unauthorized houses.

examples.ko: 무허가 노점상도 있고 허가받은 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Some street vendors are unlicensed and some are licensed.

explain: 반대말은 '허가'예요. '무허가 건물', '무허가 영업'처럼 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸미는 경우가 많아요. 일상 대화에서는 '허가 없이'라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '허가' (permission). It usually modifies a noun, as in '무허가 건물' (unauthorized building) or '무허가 영업' (unlicensed business). In daily talk people may also say '허가 없이' (without permission).

en: no grounds for charges; being cleared of suspicion

examples.en: The investigation showed there was no suspicion against him.
He received a decision of no charges.
The police announced that the person was cleared of suspicion.
His family was happy at the news that he was cleared.

examples.ko: 오랜 조사 끝에 무혐의 결정이 나왔어요.
examples.en: After a long investigation, the no-charges decision came out.

examples.ko: 무혐의라고 해서 모든 오해가 풀리는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being cleared doesn't mean every misunderstanding goes away.

explain: 뉴스에서 '무혐의 처분', '무혐의로 결론'처럼 자주 나와요. '무죄'는 재판에서 내리는 판결이고, '무혐의'는 수사 단계에서 혐의가 없다고 보는 거라서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It appears in the news in phrases like '무혐의 처분' and '무혐의로 결론'. '무죄' (not guilty) is a court verdict, while '무혐의' means the investigation found no grounds for suspicion, so they are different.

examples.en: The court invalidated that contract.
The new law nullifies the earlier decision.
The company announced that it would void the event win.
Some people suggested invalidating the vote.

examples.ko: 이미 낸 서류를 무효화하려면 어떻게 해야 해요?
examples.en: What should I do to void the documents I already submitted?

examples.ko: 한 번의 실수가 그동안의 노력을 무효화하지는 않아요.
examples.en: One mistake doesn't wipe out all the effort until now.

explain: '효력을 없애다'라는 뜻의 격식 있는 말이라서 계약, 투표, 결정, 규정처럼 공식적인 일에 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '취소하다', '없던 일로 하다'를 더 많이 말해요. 결과를 말할 때는 '무효가 되다'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is a formal word for taking away something's effect, so it is mostly used for official matters like contracts, votes, decisions and rules. In daily talk people more often say '취소하다' or '없던 일로 하다'. To describe the result, '무효가 되다' is also common.

en: absence of holidays; absence of rest

examples.ko: 이 약국은 연중무휴라서 명절에도 문을 열어요.
examples.en: This pharmacy never closes, so it's open even on holidays.

examples.ko: 연중무휴라고 쓰여 있어서 일요일에 갔는데 문이 닫혀 있었어요.
examples.en: It said open all year round, so I went on Sunday, but it was closed.
The convenience store in my neighborhood operates every day of the year.

examples.ko: 연중무휴 식당이라서 언제든 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a restaurant that never closes, so you can go anytime.
It's reassuring that there's a hospital nearby open every day.

examples.ko: 연중무휴라는 말만 믿지 말고 전화해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't just trust the 'open every day' sign; try calling.

explain: 거의 항상 '연중무휴'로 가게 앞이나 광고에서 만나요. 반대로 쉬는 날은 '휴무'나 '정기 휴무'라고 해요. 그래도 명절이나 특별한 날에는 쉬기도 하니 가기 전에 확인하면 좋아요.
explain_en: You almost always meet it as '연중무휴' (open all year) on shop signs and ads. The opposite idea is '휴무' or '정기 휴무' (regular closing day). Even so, some places still close on holidays or special days, so it's good to check before you go.
